questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: New technology that can make objects invisible
Famous stories about invisible people
Our false belief that other people don't notice us much
Why people read on crowded trains
questions.why: They discuss the 'invisibility cloak illusion': people think others don't observe them much.

questions.q: What does Dan admit about himself?
options: He watches other people a lot
He hates crowded trains
He never looks at other passengers
He always reads on the train
questions.why: Dan says he people-watches: 'I do it a lot, if I'm honest!'

questions.q: What did the survey of people in a canteen find?
options: People rarely watched anyone else while they were eating
They thought they watched others more than others watched them
People thought everyone in the room was staring at them
Men watched other people much more than women did
questions.why: Dr Loveday says people always thought they were more observational than the people watching them.

questions.q: In the waiting room experiment, what was usually true?
options: Both lists were about the same length and very similar
People refused to write the second list about themselves
The list of what the other person noticed was longer
The list of what they noticed about the other was longer
questions.why: Neil says list one, what they noticed about the other person, was always longer than list two.

questions.q: According to Dr Catherine Loveday, how do people usually observe us?
options: Very critically
Only when we look strange
Very quickly, without remembering anything
In a kind, non-judgemental way
questions.why: She says they do it 'in a non-judgemental, fairly empathic way'.

questions.q: What does Dr Loveday say about the things we feel self-conscious about?
options: Everyone notices them immediately
Other people usually don't notice them
We should try to hide them
Others notice them but are too polite to say
questions.why: She says if you're self-conscious about a spot or clothes, 'that won't be what they're noticing'.

questions.q: What is Dan's point when he mentions needing a haircut?
options: Others are probably noticing something else about him
He will get a haircut straight after the show
Neil also needs a haircut, even more than he does
People always notice bad hair before anything else
questions.why: Dan says while he's thinking about his hair, 'the other person is probably noticing something completely different'.

questions.q: How does Dan say he feels when he sees 'Simone'?
options: Angry and judgemental
Bored
Nervous and self-conscious
Completely relaxed
questions.why: Dan says he gets 'all nervous and self-conscious' when he sees her.
